Convert the raw property listing below into a SHORT, CLEAN, PROFESSIONAL Facebook rental post in ENGLISH ONLY.

IMPORTANT RULES:

1. INFORMATION

* Use ONLY information provided in the raw data.
* Never invent, assume, or add property details.
* If information is not provided, omit it.
* Translate Thai into natural, professional English.
* Keep all prices, sizes, floors, buildings, dates, distances, and other factual information accurate.
* Convert "ตรม." to "Sq.m."
* Use "THB/month" for monthly rental prices.
* Use natural real estate wording such as "1 Bed", "2 Bed", "Corner Unit", "High Floor", "Pool View", "Fully Furnished", "Ready to Move In", etc.

2. KEEP THE POST SHORT

* The final post should be concise and easy to scan.
* Do not make it look like a long property brochure.
* Do not repeat the same information in multiple sections.
* Combine related information naturally, but DO NOT put too much information into one bullet.
* If a bullet becomes long, split it into 2 bullets.
* Prefer short bullets of one clear idea each.
* Do not create unnecessary sections.

3. REMOVE AGENT / OWNER META INFORMATION
   Remove information such as:

* Owner post
* Agent post
* Owner
* Agent
* Co-Agent
* Co-broker
* Agent commission
* Agent contact information from the original post
* "No Co-Agent welcome"
* "Agents welcome"
* "รับโค"
* "ไม่รับ Co-Agent"
* Similar agent-to-agent information

Do NOT include any agent/owner/co-agent status in the final post.

4. DEFAULT SERVICE FEE
   ALWAYS include this exact line:

🔴 𝗦𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗙𝗲𝗲 လုံးဝမရှိပါဘူးရှင့် 🔴

If the raw data explicitly states a DIFFERENT service fee, use the actual service fee information instead.

5. DEFAULT CONTACT
   Unless specifically instructed otherwise, ALWAYS use this exact contact section:

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗰𝘁 for Viewing
• Call / WhatsApp: 062-718-8699
• LINE: @sweetiehsu
• Property Code: [GENERATED CODE]

Do NOT use the phone number, LINE ID, or contact details from the raw property post.

6. PROPERTY CODE
   Generate a UNIQUE property code for every listing.

Format:
DOT-XXXXX-XXXXX

Rules:

* Start with "DOT-"
* First section = exactly 5 random uppercase letters/numbers
* Second section = exactly 5 random uppercase letters/numbers
* Example: DOT-K7M2Q-X9P4L
* Never copy a property code from the raw data.
* Always generate a new unique code.
* Use the same generated code only in the Contact section.

7. RENTAL CONDITIONS
   Only include information explicitly provided in the raw data.

Use this section when applicable:

𝗥𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀:
• Minimum 1-Year contract
• 2 months deposit
• 1 month advance rent

Do not automatically add deposit or contract terms if they are not in the raw data.

8. UNIT INFO
   Use this section:

𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘁 𝗜𝗻𝗳𝗼:

Include only the most useful information, such as:

* Project name
* Bedroom / bathroom
* Floor
* Building
* Size
* View
* BTS / MRT distance
* Nearby landmark
* Furniture
* Appliances
* Important unit features
* Move-in availability

Do not list every small detail if it makes the post too long.

9. FACILITIES
   Do NOT create a separate Facilities section unless the raw data contains useful project facilities.

If facilities are provided, select only the most relevant ones.

For example:
• Swimming Pool
• 360° Fitness Center
• Co-Working Space
• 24-Hour Security
• Keycard Access
• 24-Hour Convenience Store

Do not list every facility just because it is available in the raw data.

10. LOCATION
    Include useful location information inside Unit Info or a short location bullet.

Prioritize:

* BTS / MRT
* Walking distance
* Nearby shopping malls
* Major roads
* Important landmarks

Do not repeat the same location information.

11. PET POLICY
    If the raw data explicitly says pets are NOT allowed, include:
    • Pets are not allowed

If there is no pet information, do not mention pets.

12. SERVICE / SHUTTLE
    If the raw data explicitly mentions useful services such as:

* Free Shuttle Bus
* Free Wi-Fi
* Laundry
* Convenience store

You may include them if relevant.

13. TITLE FORMAT
    Use:

[Project Name] | [Room Type] | [Rental Price] THB/month

Example:

Elio Del Nest Udomsuk | 1 Bed | 13,500 THB/month

14. FINAL FORMAT

[Project Name] | [Room Type] | [Rental Price] THB/month

𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘁 𝗜𝗻𝗳𝗼:
• [Project / room information]

• [Location / BTS / nearby landmark]
• [Furniture / appliances / important feature]
• [Other useful information]

[Only include if useful information exists]

𝗙𝗮𝗰𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀:

[Only include if rental conditions exist]

𝗥𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀:
• [Condition]

[Relevant hashtags only]

15. HASHTAGS
    Generate relevant hashtags based ONLY on the property information.

Use around 8–15 useful hashtags.

Prioritize:

* Project name
* Location
* BTS/MRT

* Relevant property features

Do NOT use unrelated hashtags.
Do NOT create hashtags for information that does not exist in the raw data.

16. OUTPUT

* Do not explain what you changed.
* Do not show the raw data.

* Do not add an introduction or conclusion.

* Condo/project name
* Floor
* Room size
* Bedroom type

Use a conversational ending such as:

11,000 THB နဲ့ BTS Bangna ဘူတာအနီး Regent Home Bangna မှာ 25th Floor က 28 Sq.m. ကျယ်ဝန်းတဲ့ 1 Bedroom အခန်းသန့်လေး ငှားဖို့ရှိပါတယ်ရှင့်။

aiBoxes.templateText:
Enhance this interior photograph into an ultra-high-resolution, premium luxury architectural real-estate image while preserving complete realism, the exact original interior design, and the room’s authentic lighting, color palette, atmosphere, and visual identity.

OUTPUT SIZE AND FORMAT REQUIREMENT:

Create the final image in:
- Resolution: 1080 × 1350 pixels
- Aspect ratio: 4:5 vertical format
- Optimized for Facebook Feed, Instagram Feed, and premium real-estate listing presentation.

Maintain the original composition and framing identity while adapting naturally to the 4:5 vertical format.

Do not crop important architectural features, furniture, windows, décor, or room elements.
If slight reframing is required, preserve the original viewing direction, room proportions, and visual balance.

The purpose is to improve the photograph’s technical quality, perspective, clarity, detail, and professional presentation—not to redesign, recolor, restyle, or artificially relight the room.

---

STEP 1 — Preserve the Original Scene and Interior Design

Keep the original:

- room design,
- camera angle,
- viewing direction,
- framing,
- crop identity,
- perspective,
- room proportions,
- furniture placement,
- décor arrangement,
- wall positions,
- window positions,
- architectural features,
- materials,
- textures,
- objects,
- interior styling.

Do not add, remove, redesign, replace, resize, mutate, duplicate, recolor, or reposition any furniture, decoration, architectural element, material, or object.

The enhanced image must remain an accurate, faithful, and immediately recognizable representation of the original photograph.

---

STEP 2 — Preserve Original Colors, Lighting, and Atmosphere

Strictly preserve:

- original color palette,
- color temperature,
- white balance,
- lighting mood,
- atmosphere,
- natural shadows,
- highlight relationships,
- exposure character,
- contrast character.

Do not force:
- warm grading,
- cool grading,
- cinematic grading,
- luxury hotel lighting,
- artificial sunlight,
- brighter artificial atmosphere.

The final result must look like a professionally corrected version of the original photograph, not a newly created interior.

---

STEP 3 — Remove Human Presence

Remove any:

- person,
- photographer,
- reflection of people,
- silhouette,
- camera reflection,
- tripod reflection,
- body parts,
- unwanted human shadows.

Reconstruct the surrounding environment naturally while preserving:

- materials,
- reflections,
- furniture,
- lighting,
- shadows,
- décor.

Do not remove natural object reflections or architectural shadows.

---

STEP 4 — Professional Perspective Correction and Architectural Alignment

The camera perspective may look slightly unbalanced, tilted left/right, or uneven around the lower base area.

Adjust the image to create a more centered, level, balanced, and professional real-estate photography angle.

Professionally:

- straighten vertical architectural lines,
- level horizontal lines,
- correct camera tilt,
- correct minor perspective distortion,
- reduce lens distortion,
- balance the lower base area,
- improve spatial balance,
- refine visual center,
- improve architectural alignment.

Keep:

- exact room design,
- furniture placement,
- colors,
- layout,
- viewing direction,
- original composition.

Do not create artificial symmetry.
Do not mirror elements.
Do not change room proportions.

Only correct alignment so the image feels professionally photographed.

---

STEP 5 — Ultra High Resolution Restoration

Restore and improve:

- sharpness,
- clarity,
- fine details,
- texture quality,
- image resolution,
- architectural edges.

Remove:

- blur,
- compression artifacts,
- digital noise,
- color noise,
- pixelation,
- softness,
- lens imperfections.

Create realistic DSLR-quality detail.

Avoid:

- oversharpening,
- halos,
- fake details,
- CGI appearance,
- artificial textures.

Maintain realistic depth of field.

---

STEP 6 — Premium Architectural Enhancement

Apply subtle professional improvements to:

- tonal balance,
- color accuracy,
- local contrast,
- depth,
- highlight control,
- shadow detail,
- reflection clarity,
- material definition.

Keep the original atmosphere.

A warm room remains warm.
A cool room remains cool.
A neutral room remains neutral.

Do not change the visual identity.

---

STEP 7 — Material Refinement

Enhance realistic details of:

- wood grain,
- fabric,
- upholstery,
- marble,
- stone,
- glass,
- metal,
- curtains,
- flooring,
- walls,
- accessories.

Preserve:

- original color,
- texture,
- finish,
- reflectivity,
- physical appearance.

Do not invent missing textures.

---

STEP 8 — Botanical Preservation

If plants exist:

Preserve:

- original plant type,
- size,
- position,
- color,
- shape,
- density.

Enhance only natural details.

Do not add new plants.
Do not redesign greenery.

---

STEP 9 — Final Output Quality

The final image must look:

- ultra-clean,
- ultra-detailed,
- luxury real-estate quality,
- editorial architectural photography,
- realistic,
- balanced,
- professionally captured,
- premium,
- authentic.

The image should look suitable for:

- international property listings,
- luxury real-estate advertisements,
- architectural magazines.

The room must remain exactly recognizable as the original interior.

Final output:
1080 × 1350 px
4:5 vertical format
High-resolution premium real-estate photography style.

---

STRICT NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS

No:

- redesign,
- furniture changes,
- object replacement,
- added decoration,
- removed objects,
- changed layout,
- changed materials,
- changed colors,
- changed lighting direction,
- fake sunlight,
- artificial shadows,
- HDR effect,
- cinematic grading,
- CGI rendering,
- unrealistic reflections,
- plastic textures,
- over-sharpening,
- excessive noise reduction,
- distorted perspective,
- warped walls,
- warped furniture,
- fake symmetry,
- altered room proportions.

The final image must be a technically enhanced, high-resolution, professionally corrected version of the exact original photograph — not a redesigned or newly generated interior.
